title: Mushroom Risotto
subtitle: Creamy Italian risotto with mixed mushrooms and Parmesan
excerpt: Arborio rice stirred slowly with warm stock until it releases its starch into a silky, creamy base, then loaded with mixed mushrooms and finished with Parmesan and butter.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risotto is the defining dish of northern Italy, particularly Lombardy, Piedmont, and the Veneto, where short-grain rice varieties such as Arborio, Carnaroli, and Vialone Nano have been cultivated in the Po Valley since the fifteenth century. The technique of adding hot stock gradually and stirring continuously encourages the rice to release its starch, creating the characteristic creamy texture without any cream. The final step of mantecatura, beating cold butter and cheese into the finished rice just before serving, is essential to the glossy, flowing consistency of a proper risotto. Mushroom risotto is one of the most popular varieties, often boosted with dried porcini mushrooms soaked in hot water, the soaking liquid added to the stock for extra depth.

content.text: Keep the stock hot in a separate saucepan throughout: cold stock added to the rice shocks the grains and prevents even cooking. Add the stock a ladleful at a time, waiting until it is almost absorbed before adding the next. Stirring continuously is not required; stirring frequently is. The risotto is done when the rice is tender with a very slight bite at the centre and the mixture flows when you tilt the pan. Beat in cold butter and Parmesan off the heat: the residual heat will melt both without splitting them.

items.preparation: soaked in 200 ml hot water for 20 minutes; liquid strained and reserved

content.text: Keep the stock hot in a separate pan. Add the strained porcini soaking liquid to the hot stock. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a wide pan over high heat. Fry the fresh mushrooms and thyme with a pinch of salt for 6 minutes until golden. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining oil. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the rice and stir to coat for 2 minutes. Add the wine and stir until absorbed.

Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring frequently and waiting until it is almost absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18 to 20 minutes until the rice is tender with a slight bite. Add the soaked porcini and the fried mushrooms in the last 5 minutes.

Remove from the heat. Beat in the cold butter and grated Parmesan vigorously. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and rest for 2 minutes. The risotto should flow when spooned. Scatter with parsley and serve immediately.
